llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed ARI client for Amazon seller action planning, with paid actions gated by quote-and-confirm steps and local API key storage.

dimensions.detail: Bash access, network calls, an ARI API key, account/balance lookups, and optional paid review collection are proportionate to the ARI workflow but should be understood before use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a local skill package with a standard-library Python CLI, no dependency installation, no remote code execution, and API calls pinned to https://ari.funewa.com with redirect blocking.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions constrain the agent to the fixed audit/action workflow, exclude ads, inventory, profit, and cash-flow decisions, and say not to run paid analysis or collection without explicit user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The CLI can persist an ARI API key to ~/.ari/config.json with 0600 permissions, but I found no scheduled tasks, background workers, tool hijacking, or broader system persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The package focuses on single-ASIN Amazon seller action planning from product details and reviews, and also exposes supporting setup, account check, review collection, and status commands that are documented in the skill materials.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use the ARI service for Amazon ASIN review/product analysis. Expect it to contact ari.funewa.com, store or read an ARI API key, show account and credit information, and spend ARI credits only after an explicit quote-and-confirm step.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The scanner's scope-mismatch concern is mostly downgraded: setup, check, collect, status, profile, quote, and run are documented in SKILL.md/README/reference materials, and collect is described as a separate step when reviews are insufficient.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced script was locally available and fully inspected in this review; I did not find evidence of analysis-evasion behavior in the artifact.
[LP1] expected: Environment key use, local key persistence, and network requests are real, but they are disclosed and tied to the ARI service workflow, with the endpoint restricted to the official HTTPS origin.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited autoconfirm behavior appears in changelog text as removed from specialized packages; the inspected CLI requires --confirm for paid collection and paid operations run.
[SQP-3] expected: The package is Chinese-first in documentation and CLI messages. This is a usability and consent clarity note, not evidence of hidden or malicious behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: The metadata prompt is broad but still points to a single-ASIN product-detail-and-review action plan, and the skill body adds narrower fixed-workflow constraints.
[SDI-2] expected: Authorization, account/balance checks, product profile reads, pricing, and paid review collection increase the trust boundary, but they are disclosed and require user-directed setup or confirmation for billable actions.
